AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered.rationale: The method is now named for the slot it belongs on and hangs on the real phase: sts2_rl/enchantments.py:315 `def after_auto_pre_play_phase_entered(self, player)`, dispatched from sts2_rl/hooks.py:485-486 `for l, fn in self._each("after_auto_pre_play_phase_entered"): fn(player)`, fired at sts2_rl/player.py:221 `self._hooks.after_auto_pre_play_phase_entered(self)` — strictly after `on_player_turn_started` (player.py:218) and after the hand draw (player.py:215), which is CombatManager.cs:556-572's PlayerTurnPhase.AutoPrePlay ordering. The extra `self.card in player.hand` clause is GONE: the body is only `if self.card is None or self.combat is None: return` / `if self.combat.turn > 1: return` / `self.combat.auto_play_card(self.card)` (enchantments.py:328-332), which is exactly src/Core/Models/Enchantments/Imbued.cs:20-26 `if (player == base.Card.Owner && player.PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber <= 1) await CardCmd.AutoPlay(choiceContext, base.Card, null);` — no pile check on either side. The turn gate is equivalent: sts2_rl/combat.py:109 sets `self.turn = 1` at combat start and combat.py:825/836 increment it, so `turn > 1` fires exactly once, on turn 1. `auto_play_card` (sts2_rl/combat.py:621-640) pulls the card out of hand, draw, discard or exhaust, so the bottom-of-draw-pile sink does not block it. The enchantment is a live listener (sts2_rl/combat.py:131-134 registers `card.enchantment` for every deck card), so the surface has a real consumer. EXECUTED today from the repo root: `py audit/tools/enchantment_probes.py imbued` prints `MATCH Imbued auto-play fired on N of 20 opening hands: sim=20 C#=20` (was sim=0 when the issue was written).  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: STILL OPEN, and the witness has moved the WRONG WAY. Imbued.cs:20-25 is `if (player == Card.Owner && player.PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber <= 1) await CardCmd.AutoPlay(ctx, Card, null);` -- NO pile check -- and the sim STILL adds `self.card in player.hand` (enchantments.py:315-321), and still hangs the body on `on_player_turn_started` rather than the `after_auto_pre_play_phase_entered` slot that now exists (hooks.py:480-486; see this record's BR-4 guard). Now that the turn-1 bottom-of-draw-pile pass IS ported (player.py:193-207, which closed BR-5), the Imbued card is GUARANTEED not to be in the opening hand, so the extra guard can never pass. EXECUTED 2026-07-28 (`py audit/tools/enchantment_probes.py imbued`): over seeds 0-19 with a 10-card deck holding one Imbued Defend the sim's auto-play fired on 0 of 20 openings; before the sink pass landed it was 7 of 20, and the game is 20 of 20. The fix is to drop the hand guard and rename the method to `after_auto_pre_play_phase_entered`. LIVE: granted by the ported Electric Shrymp relic (relics/electric_shrymp.py:17-21), and combat.auto_play already handles a card that is not in hand (`if card in self.player.hand: remove`, combat.py:516-517), so nothing but the guard is stopping it.

guards.what: FOUR-VERB COVERAGE (enchant / upgrade+downgrade / transform / copy) -- stated explicitly so the hole cannot reopen silently. Verb 3, TRANSFORM: CardCmd.Transform (CardCmd.cs:369-451) removes the original from its pile and adds a freshly-built replacement; it never touches Enchantment, and the destroyed original takes its enchantment with it
guards.maps_to: TRANSFORM verdict: FAITHFUL, both engines drop the enchantment. C#: CardCmd.Transform's loop takes `item.GetReplacement(rng)`, calls `item.Original.RemoveFromCurrentPile()` (CardCmd.cs:400) and adds the replacement (CardCmd.cs:437/440); the word Enchantment does not appear anywhere in the method, and neither AfterTransformedFrom nor AfterTransformedTo (CardModel.cs:1625-1631, both empty virtuals -- SovereignBlade is the only override in the source) moves it. So the enchantment dies with the original. SIM: run.transform_card (run.py:725-801) and CardCmd.transform_to_random (cmds.py:1467-1538) both build the replacement with `make_card(...)`, which carries no enchantment. EXECUTED, this unit: `py -c "import sys,random;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.run import RunState;from sts2_rl.cards import make_card;from sts2_rl.enchantments import make_enchantment;r=RunState(rng=random.Random(0));c=make_card('defend');r.deck=[c];e=make_enchantment('imbued');e.amount=2;e.attach(c);n=r.transform_card(c,into=make_card('bash'));print(n.id, n.enchantment)"` -> `bash None`, matching C#. The in-combat twin (CardCmd.transform_to_random on a Sharp'd Strike) also prints a replacement with `enchantment=None`. Same result for all 17 ids. COVERAGE TABLE for this unit -- (1) ENCHANT: the CanEnchantCardType hook entry plus the reachability guard above. (2) UPGRADE / DOWNGRADE: cannot bite here, and that is now executed rather than assumed: `py -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.enchantments import ALL_ENCHANTMENTS, Enchantment;print(sorted(k for k,v in ALL_ENCHANTMENTS.items() if v.attach is not Enchantment.attach))"` -> `['goopy','souls','steady','tezcataras_ember']`. Only those four override attach() to mutate a static card property (exhausts / retain / cost / eternal), so only those four can be undone by the card rebuild that upgrade()/downgrade() performs. This unit is not one of them -- it works through the modify_* hooks, which are read live off the still-attached enchantment -- so upgrade and downgrade are no-ops for it. (3) TRANSFORM: this entry, faithful. (4) COPY: guard EG2, gap. All four verbs are now on the record; before this pass transform and copy were 0/17.
